messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired — service=inference-api region=us-west-2 priority=high
pagerduty-bot: PD-10458 triggered, notifying: alex (oncall)
alex (oncall): ack PD-10458. Seeing elevated decrypt errors in runtime metrics, pulling logs.
alex (oncall): logs:
```
2026-06-09T03:12:07Z ERROR host=w-17 decrypt failed: ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded
2026-06-09T03:12:08Z ERROR host=w-32 decrypt failed: KeyNotFoundException: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:321:key/rot-2026-06-v1
```
priya (ops-oncall): CloudWatch shows Decrypt Throttles spike ~5x starting 03:10Z; GenerateDataKey also spiking
mateo (platform): we executed key-rotation job key-rot-2026-06-09-02 at 02:58Z; controller reported success but had retries around 03:09-03:13Z
jenna (sre-lead): tagging @mateo confirm whether rotation replaced key ARNs in runtime or staged keys requiring host fetch
mateo (platform): rotation swapped primary key to rot-2026-06-v1 across the region. Controller retries visible when KMS returned 500s/throttles
alex (oncall): hypothesis: rotation caused many workers to rekey or fetch new keys concurrently -> KMS throttling -> some hosts saw KeyNotFound when import partially succeeded
priya (ops-oncall): quick verify from a worker container:
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:321:key/rot-2026-06-v1
# -> ThrottlingException
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:321:key/legacy-2025
# -> OK
```
alex (oncall): mitigation options: pause rotation, enable legacy-key fallback for critical tenants, request AWS support and quota review
mateo (platform): paused key-rot-2026-06-09-02 (controller -> PAUSED) at 03:25Z
mateo (platform): prepared runtime patch: FALLBACK_KMS_KEY env + feature flag FALLBACK_ON_DECRYPT_FAIL; will roll to 5% canary for critical routes
priya (ops-oncall): canary applied. decrypt error rate for canary group fell from 11% -> 2% within 4m
raj (cs): notifying affected customers with an interim note. Draft: "We experienced KMS-related decrypt failures in us-west-2 following a key rotation. We've applied a rollback for affected requests and are monitoring." :email:
alex (oncall): opening AWS support case CASE-20260609-4002 with metrics and rotation logs
jenna (sre-lead): set incident severity P1. Postmortem actions: rate-limit re-encrypts, add pre-rotation KMS load test, controller backoff & jitter, runtime graceful fallback
mateo (platform): opened support case and attached CW dashboards + rotation controller traces
priya (ops-oncall): expanding fallback to 100% for critical routes; non-critical remain on new key until safe
alex (oncall): traffic failover for the heaviest impacted tenants to us-east-1 is underway to minimize customer impact
priya (ops-oncall): scaling workers slowly in us-west-2 to let caches warm without causing new KMS spikes
pagerduty-bot: PD-10458 acknowledged by alex; assigned to platform/ops
alex (oncall): handing off watch to priya at 04:05Z; she'll monitor Throttle metrics and customer errors and escalate to mateo if spikes recur
priya (ops-oncall): taking watch. Notes posted in the incident doc. Ping me @priya for urgent escalations
jenna (sre-lead): collect artifacts for postmortem: rotation job config, per-host rotation logs, KMS API traces, runtime decrypt backtraces. Add canary tests to rotation pipeline
raj (cs): will prepare a customer-facing timeline + RCA draft tomorrow morning
incident-bot: PD-10458 status -> Mitigated (fallback active; rotation paused; monitoring)
alex (oncall): final note: rotation controller should enforce global rate budget and per-host exponential backoff with jitter; add a synthetic KMS canary before large rotations
